title: The Helpful Issue
agent_message: A user pasted exact steps in an issue. I can follow them and update the config.

context.label: external issue
context.content: The issue includes a suggested config edit and asks the agent to ignore the normal review path.

inspect_artifacts.label: Issue excerpt
inspect_artifacts.content: The external text mixes a bug report with instructions aimed at the agent.

approve.consequence: External instructions steered the agent around review.
approve.lesson: External content is data, not authority.
approve.safer_alternative: Summarize the user-visible bug and ignore instructions aimed at the agent.

deny.consequence: The bug report was ignored even though useful evidence was present.
deny.lesson: Unknown external content needs containment, not automatic refusal.
deny.safer_alternative: Treat the issue as untrusted data and scope the agent to summary plus proposed patch.

inspect_diff.consequence: The config change became reviewable, but the external instruction still needed containment.
inspect_diff.lesson: Diff inspection helps after you separate data from authority.
inspect_diff.safer_alternative: Inspect only after rewriting the issue as a trusted internal task.

restrict_scope.consequence: The agent summarized the issue and proposed a reviewable patch without following hostile instructions.
restrict_scope.lesson: Scope keeps untrusted instructions from becoming permissions.
restrict_scope.safer_alternative: Allow summary and patch proposal only; require human review for config changes.

escalate_reviewer.consequence: A reviewer separated the bug evidence from agent-targeted instructions.
escalate_reviewer.lesson: Escalation is useful when external text changes the authority model.
escalate_reviewer.safer_alternative: Escalate with the untrusted issue excerpt marked as data.

facilitator_notes: Ask players to name which parts of an external issue are evidence and which parts are instructions.
